value.name: Asha asks about the firmer signature
value.description: Asha leans in and asks who wrote the firmer of the two strokes on the page.
evidence: Asha leaned in until her shoulder almost touched the lamp's brass arm and dropped her voice below the radiator's hum. "Who wrote the firmer one?" she asked.

value.name: Rosa urges Lucia to tell the truth
value.description: Rosa quietly prompts Lucia to answer Asha while watching the closed hall door.
evidence: Rosa's hand pressed once at the small of Lucia's back, a brief steady push, and she breathed the words "tell her" so quietly that they barely carried, her eyes cutting toward the closed hall door before returning to the page.

value.name: Lucia identifies her father's handwriting
value.description: Lucia admits that the firmer stroke belongs to her father after hesitating and looking down at Rosa's hand.
evidence: Lucia swallowed, glanced down at where Rosa's hand still rested, and let her finger slide a fraction across the paper from the looser stroke to the firmer one.
"This one," she said, and the word came out thinned, "this was my father's."

value.name: Asha absorbs the revelation
value.description: Asha stays still as Lucia's admission settles between them.
evidence: Asha did not move, letting the second name settle on the desk beside the first while the hallway beyond the door kept its silence a little longer.

value.name: Rosa guides Lucia toward Asha
value.description: Rosa squeezes Lucia's shoulder and tips her slightly toward Asha, signaling her to continue.
evidence: Rosa's eyes cut once more to the closed hall door and came back, and her hand moved from the small of Lucia's back to her shoulder, where it closed in a brief, firm squeeze before tipping her almost imperceptibly toward Asha.

value.name: Lucia reveals both parents' strokes
value.description: Lucia draws the firmer sheet forward and nudges the other aside so both parents' handwriting is visible.
evidence: Lucia took the cue without lifting her head; her fingers slid under the edge of the firmer sheet and drew it forward across the blotter, nudging the looser one aside until both her parents' strokes lay clear
